title: SCUMMVM
subtitle: The ScummVM team, 2004 · 0.6.1 with Beneath a Steel Sky (Revolution, 1994, freeware) — C++ over SDL 1.2
argsHint: -p<dir> where the game is, then its name. Other switches of 0.6.1: -g<scaler> (normal, 2x, 3x, 2xsai, super2xsai, supereagle, advmame2x, advmame3x, hq2x, hq3x, tv2x, dotmatrix), -f for full screen, -m<volume> for the music, -s<volume> for the sound effects, -n to show subtitles (off by default; with speech, the text is shown too).
fpsNote: A FALLBACK cap only: the engine paces itself on the SDL clock.

needsData.hint: sky-cd/ from bass-cd-1.0.zip (sky.dsk and sky.dnr), the freeware CD version the ScummVM project distributes

controls: the control panel: save, load, quit
_why: The first program here whose C++ is a whole engine rather than a part of a game: namespaces, function templates with value parameters (its scalers, one instance per pixel format), an explicit specialisation, a class with two polymorphic bases (every GUI button), pointers to member functions (Sky's table of actions) and dynamic_cast, each added to src/cxx and held to g++ by tools/gate-cxx.mjs. The game is drawn in 8 bits, scaled into a 16-bit display by ScummVM's own scalers, and its music and speech come through SDL_OpenAudio's callback.
